ImageDescription.value:
The Chicago Lakefront Trail (LFT) is a 18.5-mile-long (29.8 km) partial shared use path for walking, jogging, skateboarding, and cycling, located along the western shore of Lake Michigan in Chicago, Illinois. The trail passes through and connects Chicago's four major lakefront parks along with various beaches and recreational amenities. It also serves as a route for bicycle, skateboard and personal transporter commuters. On busy summer days 70,000 people use the trail.

The LFT is located wholly within the Chicago city limits and spans from 7100 South/2560 East to 5800 North/1000 West. It is a dedicated-use path, although frequent intersections do pose a threat to path users. These intersections are clearly signed both to path users and motorists. From north to south, it runs through Lincoln Park, Grant Park, Burnham Park, and Jackson Park.

Some attractions along the path (listed from south to north) are the South Shore Cultural Center, the Museum of Science and Industry, McCormick Place, Soldier Field, Chicago's Museum Campus, Monroe Harbor, Navy Pier, Belmont Harbor, and the Waveland Clock Tower. The Lakefront Trail connects most of the Chicago beaches and three skate parks (31st Street, Grant Park, Wilson Avenue). Several dog parks are accessible from the trail.

Path maintenance is provided by the Chicago Park District. The Lakefront Trail is open 24 hours a day, but the parks and beaches along the path close at 11 PM.

ObjectName.value: Chicago Lakefront Trail 2023-09-09

Categories.value: CC-Zero|875 North Michigan Avenue|Self-published work|Images with extracted images|United States photographs taken on 2023-09-09|September 2023 in Chicago|Lakefront Trail (Chicago)|Taken with iPhone 13

ImageDescription.value: The Chicago Lakefront Trail as it appeared in on a partly sunny morning in September 2023 just north Magnificent Mile and the John Hancock Center. It is an 18.5-mile scenic path running along the western shore of Lake Michigan, offering stunning views of both the lake and the city skyline. It stretches from Ardmore Avenue in Edgewater on the north to 71st Street in South Shore on the south, passing through several of Chicago’s major parks, including Lincoln Park, Grant Park, Burnham Park, and Jackson Park. The trail has separate lanes for pedestrians and cyclists, enhancing safety and comfort for all users. The northern section offers access to Lincoln Park Zoo, North Avenue Beach, and Belmont Harbor, with tree-lined paths and open spaces ideal for cycling. As the trail passes through downtown Chicago, it provides views of Millennium Park, Navy Pier, and the Museum Campus, with the Navy Pier Flyover allowing cyclists to bypass busy intersections safely. Heading south, the trail passes the Museum of Science and Industry, McCormick Place, Soldier Field, and the South Shore Cultural Center, with Burnham Park offering beaches and recreational areas. The trail is accessible at numerous points along its route, open year-round, and maintained by the Chicago Park District to ensure a pleasant experience.
